column1: # Public datasets Akshar trains and evaluates on.
# Every file is pinned to an upstream revision and verified by SHA-256 (the
# upstream Git LFS object id) before anything reads it.  `scripts/fetch-data.sh`
# downloads into data/raw/<set>/<name>; `make data-fetch` is the entry point.
# Scope: every language Aksharantar publishes in the Devanagari script.
# Kashmiri (kas) and Sindhi (sid) are Perso-Arabic there and are not listed.
# The pairs train the engine and measure it per language (official
# train/valid/test splits); only the trained model ships, never this data.
#   aksharantar   manually collected pairs CC-BY 4.0; mined (Samanantar,
#                 IndicCorp) and existing-source pairs CC0.  Madhani et al.,
# Columns (tab-separated): set  name  bytes  sha256  licence  url
# IndicCorp v2 sample (AI4Bharat, CC0; Doddapaneni et al., "Towards Leaving
# No Indic Language Behind", ACL 2023): monolingual text from which the
# per-language word-frequency lists are counted.  Only the counts ship.
# The full Devanagari files are ~113 GB, so large files are SAMPLED: evenly
# spaced 25 MiB byte ranges (7th column), 12 per language (Hindi: 4 from
# each of its three files), ~300 MiB per language; the offsets are
# floor(i * (size - 25 MiB) / 11).  Maithili, Bodo and Dogri are small and
# fetched whole, pinned by the upstream Git LFS hash.  A slice's SHA-256 is
# of its own bytes; slices start/end mid-line, which the counter discards.
